definition.inputDomain: Integer 0..100000; 0 and 1 have no phase and are neither prime nor composite.
definition.mathematicalDomain: All integers n >= 2; native computation is capped at100000.
definition.quadrantDecision: Exact x>0 and y>0 (quadrant I) iff prime on the mathematical domain.
definition.residueRestriction: R=0 for primes; R=1 for composites>4; R=3 for n=4.
definition.rotation: Display only: axes and points rotate together. The decision uses canonical exact coordinates.

verification.scope: Finite checks support the implementation. The global equivalence follows from Wilson and the composite factorial lemma.

limits: This is a proved Wilson-derived phase encoding, not an independently discovered zeta rule.
It retains the cost of the modular factorial; no speedup or RH consequence is claimed.
Pixel colors and rounded angles are visual evidence only; exact coordinate signs decide.
The45-degree margin is in phase space. A rendered image must still resolve the point and axes.
